rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Coming is for reckoning and recompense; the past form depicts a certain future, as in 16:1.
rows.anchor: للحساب والجزاء وهو بمعنى المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to Quraysh, revealed after they boasted of wealth and children and mocked the poor, claiming they would not be punished in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: والخطاب لكفار قريش لأنها نزلت حين قالوا افتخارا واستخفافا للفقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فرادى is plural of فرد: each person stands alone, separated from wealth, children, and worldly things they preferred.
rows.anchor: {فرادى} جمع فرد أي منفردين عن الأموال والأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison may be appositive to فرادى or a circumstantial phrase describing their solitude.
rows.anchor: بدل من فرادى أي على الهيئة التي ولدتم عليها في الانفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are resurrected as first created: naked, barefoot, uncircumcised, and without conditions acquired in earthly life.
rows.anchor: مشبهين ابتداء خلقكم عراة حفاة غرلا بهما

rows.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها والرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Aisha exclaimed at men and women being resurrected naked; the Prophet replied each would be too occupied to look at the other sex.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها واسوءتاه الرجل والمرأة كذلك فقال عليه السلام : "لكل امرىء منهم يومئذ شأن يغنيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God bestowed was worldly property that distracted people from the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ما تفضلنا به عليكم في الدنيا فشغلتم به عن الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takhwīl is either ownership of retainers and servants, or a gift granted without recompense.
rows.anchor: والتخويل تمليك الخول ، أي : الخدم والأتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They left behind what they had not sent ahead as good deeds; unlike believers, whose sound beliefs and righteous works accompany them to the gathering, so they are not truly alone.
rows.anchor: ما قدمتم منه شيئا ولم تحملوا نقيرا بخلاف المؤمنين فإنهم صرفوا همتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supposed intercessors are the idols.
rows.anchor: الأصنام {الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاؤا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They claimed the idols shared God's lordship over them and right to be worshiped.
rows.anchor: شركاء الله في ربوبيتكم واستحقاق عبادتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means severance occurred between them, by analogy with the idiom that a joining was made between two things.
rows.anchor: وقع التقطع بينكم كما يقال جمع بين الشيئين

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi glosses this as the bond and affection between them having been severed.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (منقطع كشت آنه ميان شما بود ازوصلت ومودت)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ضل عنكم means that what they relied on became void and was lost.
rows.anchor: وضل عنكم} أي : بطل وضاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that they claimed their idols were intercessors, but the idols cannot avert punishment.
rows.anchor: أنها شفعاؤكم فلم يقدروا على دفع شيء من العذاب عنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively they claimed the idols were partners in lordship; the author prefers this sense because it fits the preceding mention of alleged partners.
rows.anchor: أو أنها شركاؤكمفي ربوبيتكم وهو الأنسب لسياق النظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person's four enemies are wealth, family, children, and friends; none enter the grave with the dead.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن للإنسان أعداء أربعة هي : المال والأهل والأولاد والأصدقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four companions entering the grave and interceding are the testimony of faith, prayer, fasting, and remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: وأصدقاء أربعة هي : كلمة الشهادة والصلاة والصوم وذكر الله هي تدخل في القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wise person prepares for solitude by acquiring taqwa as clothing and righteous action as a companion.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يتفكر في تجرده وتفرده فيسعى في تحصيل لباس له هو التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says good deeds comfort, brighten, protect, and enlarge the grave; evil deeds frighten, darken, constrict, and torment their owner.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إن عمل الإنسان يدفن معه في قبره

rows.speaker: اليافعي
rows.claim: Al-Yafi‘i heard of a Yemeni righteous man who saw a black dog leave a grave after burial; the dog was the dead person's deeds, while Yasin and its companion sūras protected the deceased and drove it away.
rows.anchor: قال اليافعي : وقد سمعت عن بعض الصالحين في بعض بلاد اليمن

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Sa‘di's verses teach worldly grief and joy pass, while deeds and a good name remain; possessions and status are no lasting support.
rows.anchor: غم وشادماني نماند وليك جزاى عمل ماندو نام نيك

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri says people enter and leave the world detached; ties and burdens accumulate, but wealth, status, and intercessors cannot rescue them at God's reckoning; their bonds, hopes, and efforts fail.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري : {ولقد جئتمونا فرادى} أي : دخلتم الدنيا بخرقة وخرجتم منها بخرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The journey to God proceeds through tajrīd, tafrīd, then tawḥīd. Tajrīd detaches from this world; tafrīd frees one from attachment to both worlds, as the spirit was before embodiment.
rows.anchor: والإشارة أن المجيء إلى الله يكون بالتجريد ثم بالتفريد ثم بالتوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first creation is the spirit before attachment to the body; he links this to embryonic creation in 23:14 and creation and forming in 7:11.
rows.anchor: كما كان في بدء الخلقة روحا مجردا عن تعلقات الكونين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeker strives to detach from both realms; worldly gifts signify their attachments. Supposed intercessors are deeds and states thought to lead to God, severed at journey's end.
rows.anchor: فللعبد في السير إلى الله كسب وسعي بالتجريد والتفريد عن الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The journey ends at divine majesty, as Gabriel's ascent ended at the Lote Tree, the limit for angelic and human travelers. Tawḥīd receives divine oneness and joins the servant to unity.
rows.anchor: فإذا وصل العبد إلى سرادقات العزة انتهى سيره كما انتهى سير جبرائيل ليلة المعراج عند سدرة المنتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without primordial divine care, the seeker would stop at the Lote Tree, saying each has a known station, as in 37:164.
rows.anchor: ولو لم تدركه العناية الأزلية بجذبات الربوبية لانقطع عن السير في الله بالله وبقي في السدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God first created Adam from clay without his particular form, then formed him; the plural attributes all descendants' creation and shaping to their forefather, since his creation aimed at populating earth through them.
rows.anchor: خلقنا أباكم آدم طينا غير مصور بصورته المخصوصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural attribution is figurative: Adam's creation and shaping are treated as the creation and shaping of his descendants.
rows.anchor: فكان خلقه بمنزلة خلق أولاده فالإسناد في ضمير الجمع مجازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command addressed all the angels because the wording is general and no restricting evidence is given.
rows.anchor: {ثم قلنا للملائكة} كلهم لعموم اللفظ وعدم المخصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prostration was greeting and honor; ritual prostration with intent to worship is directed only to God.
rows.anchor: {اسجدوا لادم} سجدة تحية وتكريم ؛ لأن السجود الشرعي وهو وضع الجبهة على قصد العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels prostrated without delay or hesitation.
rows.anchor: {فسجدوا} أي : الملائكة بعد الأمر من غير تلعثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلا إبليس here means لكن إبليس, introducing an exception as but.
rows.anchor: {إلا إبليس} أي : لكن إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He was not among those prostrating to Adam, though he had prostrated to God.
rows.anchor: {لم يكن من الساجدين} أي : ممن سجد لآدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ألا means أن تسجد, with لا treated as extra, as in 57:29, where لئلا conveys that the People of the Book may know.
rows.anchor: أي : أن تسجدو لا صلة كما في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command refers to the time God ordered Iblis to prostrate.
rows.anchor: إذ أمرتك} أي : وقت أمري إياك به

words: أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِى مِن نَّارٍۢ وَخَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن طِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis claimed superiority because fire is subtle and luminous while clay is dense and dark; the author says he erred by judging virtue from material and element.
rows.anchor: والنار جوهر لطيف نوراني ، والطين جسم كثيف ظلماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian verses contrast Adam's outward form with divine light, warning against judging by appearance while ignoring spiritual meaning.
rows.anchor: زآدمي إبليس صورت ديد وبس غافل ازمعنى شد آن مردود خس

words: خَلَقْتَنِى مِن نَّارٍۢ وَخَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن طِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Masnavi has fire claim superiority over clay, but God's answer makes piety the measure of merit, not lineage.
rows.anchor: كفت نار ازخاك بي شك بهترست

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Adam's honor and virtue over the angels were not simply due to properties of clay or to being kneaded without an intermediary.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : أن شرف مسجودية آدم وفضيلته على ساجديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem warns against relying on analogy when the sun of certainty or Kaaba is present, urging submission to God's superior knowledge.
rows.anchor: ليك با خورشيد وكعبه يش رو اين قياس واين تحرى را مجو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage cites a report that God forgives believers' mountain-sized sins and places them on Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: بذنوب أمثال الجبال فيغفرها الله لهم ويضعها على اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says it accords with divine favor toward believers to ransom them through unbelievers: justice toward sinners and grace toward the obedient, against Mu'tazila denial.
rows.anchor: ولا يستبعد من فضل الله مع أهل الإسلام والإيمان أن يفديهم بأهل الكفر والطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mu'tazila cite 6:164, but 29:13 says unbelievers bear their own and additional burdens; each unbeliever is still punished for their own sin.
rows.anchor: فلا يصح استدلالهم بالآية لأن كل كافر معاقب بوزره والله أعلم بحقيقة الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God addressed Adam after expelling Iblis from the Garden.
rows.anchor: {ويااادم} أي : وقلنا لآدم بعد إخراج إبليس من الجنة يا آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means reside in a way that permits their stay and honors them.
rows.anchor: أي : لازم الإقامة على طريق الإباحة والتكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam's spouse is Eve.
rows.anchor: حواء والزوج في كلام العرب هو العدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic زوج can mean the single counterpart in a pair; two companions are called زوجان.
rows.anchor: والزوج في كلام العرب هو العدد الفرد المزاوج لصاحبه فأما الاثنان المصطحبان

rows.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
rows.claim: Most scholars hold this is the Garden of eternal recompense.
rows.anchor: جنة الخلد التي جعلت دار الجزاء وعليه أكثر أهل العلم لوجوه ذكروها في كتبهم

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين من أهل الظاهر والباطن
rows.claim: Some careful outward and inward scholars say it was either a garden in heaven from which they descended or an earthly garden elevated above the surrounding land.
rows.anchor: أو جنة في السماء هبطا منها أو جنة في الأرض كانت مرتفعة على سائر بقاع الأرض

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين من أهل الظاهر والباطن
rows.claim: They argue it was a test garden: the final Garden has no prohibition; Adam slept, was expelled, and Iblis entered, unlike the Garden of recompense.
rows.anchor: لأنه كلف فيها أن لا يأكل من تلك الشجرة ولا تكليف في الجنة الجزائية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Adam craved grapes from the Garden at death; his sons went to find them, but angels met them and tended to Adam's burial.
rows.anchor: ولما روي أن آدم لما احتضر اشتهى قطفا من عنب الجنة فانطلق بنوه ليطلبوه فلقيتهم الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He concludes Adam's garden was on earth: his sons sought its grapes, and the Nile is said to emerge from the Garden, which he identifies with earthly gardens.
rows.anchor: وقد ثبت أن النيل يخرج من الجنة ولا شك أنها من جنان الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pair could eat wherever they wished and freely enjoy the Garden's fruits and blessings.
rows.anchor: من أي مكان شئتما ، ومن أي شيء شئتما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God left the tree unidentified; if naming it benefited people, He would have specified it, as Akam al-Marjan says.
rows.anchor: اختلفوا في هذه الشجرة أيضا وقد أبهم الله ذكرها وتعيينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Becoming wrongdoers means wronging themselves.
rows.anchor: أي : فتصيرا من الذين ظلموا أنفسهم

rows.speaker: الصحاح
rows.claim: Al-Sihah says the verb means whispering to them, though لهما is used where إليهما might be expected; Arabs connect this verb with all these prepositions.
rows.anchor: قال في "الصحاح" : فوسوس لهما الشيطان يريد إليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswasa is repeated, quiet speech Satan casts into a human heart to make religiously forbidden conduct seem attractive.
rows.anchor: والوسوسة : الكلام الخفي المكرر يلقيه الشيطان إلى قلب البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan first mourned to sadden them; when asked why, he said he pitied their coming death and separation from blessings, and the idea settled in their hearts.
rows.anchor: وأول ما ابتدأهما به من كيده إياهما أنه ناح عليهما نياحة أحزنتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ليبدي means to make manifest.
rows.anchor: {ليبدي لهما} أي : ليظهر لهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is consequential: Satan aimed at sin, and exposing their nakedness was the result rather than his intended purpose.
rows.anchor: واللام للعاقبة لأن اللعين إنما وسوس لهما ليوقعهما في المعصية لا لظهور عورتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the lām states his purpose: Satan meant to humiliate them by exposing their nakedness before angels; he knew of it from reading angelic books, while Adam did not.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون اللام لام الغرض على أنه أراد بوسوسته أن يسوءهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This aim shows that uncovering private parts in solitude or before one's spouse without need is naturally disgraceful.
rows.anchor: وفي كون الانكشاف غرضا لإبليس دليل على أن كشف العورة في الخلوة وعند الزوج من غير حاجة

rows.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Ali reportedly avoided looking at his own nakedness, fearing he might see it with the same eye by which he saw the Prophet's beauty.
rows.anchor: ولم يقع نظر علي رضي الله عنه إلى عورته حذرا من أن يراها بالعين التي يرى بها جمال رسول الله

rows.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
rows.claim: Aisha said neither she nor the Prophet ever saw the other's nakedness.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها "ما رأى مني ولا رأيت منه" أي العورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما ووري refers to what was concealed from them; وارى is an unfamiliar passive form here.
rows.anchor: أي : الذي ستر عنهما وهو مجهول واري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their private parts were hidden by their clothing; neither could see them on themselves or the other.
rows.anchor: وكانا لا يريانها من أنفسهما ولا أحدهما من الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural سوءات may avoid using the dual twice, or count each person's anus and vulva separately, making four.
rows.anchor: والسوءات جمع السوءة والتعبير بلفظ الجمع عن اثنين لكراهة اجتماع لفظي التثنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The private part is called سوءة because exposure distresses a person.
rows.anchor: وسميت العورة سوءة ؛ لأنه يسوء الإنسان انكشافها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وقال is coordinated with وسوس and elaborates how Satan whispered.
rows.anchor: وقال} عطف على وسوس بيانا وتفصيلا لكيفية وسوسته

words: مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan meant that their Lord forbade eating from the tree for some reason.
rows.anchor: أي : عن أكلها لأمر ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan said the prohibition was dislike of their becoming angel-like, with subtle bodies and no need for food or drink; angelic superiority in some respects does not establish absolute superiority over prophets.
rows.anchor: أي : كالملائكة في لطافة البنية والاستغناء عن التغذي بالأطعمة والأشربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suggestion is not that humans could become angelic in essence, which the author calls impossible.
rows.anchor: فليس المراد انقلاب حقيقتهما البشرية إلى الحقيقة الملكية فإنه محال

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Saadi the Mufti objects that Ash‘aris allow such a transformation because bodies are homogeneous.
rows.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي : فيه بحث إذ لا مانع منه عند الأشاعرة لتجانس الأجسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God distinguished angels, jinn, and humans by form: changing a human's inner and outer constitution makes them no longer human, while angels and devils retain their nature through outward transformations.
rows.anchor: فمن حصل على بنية الإنسان ظاهرا وباطنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The khalidīn never die and remain forever in the Garden.
rows.anchor: {أو تكونا من الخالدين} الذين لا يموتون ويخلدون في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their ancestors' practice refers to attachment to worldly life and its desires.
rows.anchor: {قالوا وجدنا عليهآ ءابآءنا} أي : على محبة الدنيا وشهواتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They construed God's command as permission to pursue worldly goods through lawful earning.
rows.anchor: {والله أمرنا بها} أي : بطلبها بالكسب الحلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not command love of the world or greed for accumulation; He permits lawful earnings needed to sustain the body and clothes for worship.
rows.anchor: لا يأمر بحب الدنيا والحرص على جمعها وإنما يأمر بالكسب الحلال

words: أَتَقُولُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: They fabricate claims about God without knowing the consequences or recognizing the devil's temptation and embellishment.
rows.anchor: أي : تفترون على الله ما لا تعلمون آفته ولاوبال عاقبته ولا تعلمون أن ذلك من فتنة الشيطان وتزيينه وإغوائه كذا في "التأويلات النجمية".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Masnavi calls this world carrion, a worthless corpse over which people should not be greedy.
rows.anchor: اين جهان جيفهاست ومردار رخيص برنين مردار ون باشم حريص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qist means justice and the balanced middle of a thing, beyond excess and deficiency.
rows.anchor: والقسط العدل وهو الوسط من كل شيء المتجاوز عن طرفي الإفراط والتفريط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the best matters are in the middle; a Persian verse likewise says both extremes are blameworthy.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر "خير الأمور أوساطها"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وأقيموا is coordinated with أمر with an implied قل, avoiding coordination of an imperative with an indicative.
rows.anchor: معطوف على أمر بتقدير قل لئلا يلزم عطف الإنشاء على الأخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means either turn steadfastly toward worship without turning elsewhere, or face the qibla.
rows.anchor: أو أقيموا وجوهكم نحو القبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عند كل مسجد may denote a time or place; sujūd stands for the whole prayer by naming a part for the whole.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون اسم زمان ، وأن يكون اسم مكان أي في كل وقت سجود

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says to pray at whichever mosque one reaches when prayer time comes, rather than insist on one's own; if none is nearby, go to any mosque.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : معناه إذا حضرت الصلاة وأنتم في مسجد فصلوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Furūʿ says the neighborhood mosque is preferable to the congregational mosque if its imam is learned; market workers should pray by the shop by day and home at night.
rows.anchor: وفي الفروع : مسجد المحلة أفضل من الجامع إذا كان الإمام عالما

rows.speaker: الحدادي
rows.claim: Al-Haddadi reads the verse as requiring obligatory prayer in congregation; a hadith exempts those with an excuse who hear the call but do not answer.
rows.anchor: قال الحدادي : وهذه الآية تدل على وجوب فعل الصلاة المكتوبة في الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Congregational prayer earns 27 degrees over solitary prayer, associated with 17 obligatory and 10 regular daily rak‘ahs.
rows.anchor: وصلاة الجماعة أفضل من صلاة الفذ بسبع وعشرين درجة

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars say mosque prayer is better than home congregation for rites such as obligatory prayer and tarawih because it displays Islam's symbols; home congregation exceeds praying alone at home.
rows.anchor: قال العلماء : كل ما شرعت فيه الجماعة كالفرائض والتراويح ونحوهما فالمسجد فيه أفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دعاء means worship here: a specific act names the broader category; supplication is a gateway to worship, whose core is humble dependence on God.
rows.anchor: أي : واعبدوه فهو من إطلاق الخاص على العام فإن الدعاء من أبواب العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dīn means obedience, since people return to God in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أي : الطاعة فإن مصيركم إليه في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian verse warns the traveler not to be deceived when reality becomes clear after performing only metaphorical or insincere acts.
rows.anchor: فردا كه يشكاه حقيقت شود بديد شر منده رهروى كه عمل بر مجاز كرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God originated you and will recreate you for judgment; the comparison describes an omitted verbal noun, returning as He first created you.
rows.anchor: {كما بدأكم} أي : أنشأكم ابتداء {تعودون} إليه بإعادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection is possible: whoever originated creation can repeat it, and raising people is no harder than creating them initially.
rows.anchor: وإنما شبه الإعادة بالإبداء تقريرا لإمكانها والقدرة عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rajfa was a severe earthquake; Hud calls their destruction a cry, possibly preceding the quake, so the end is attributed once to a near cause and once to a remote one.
rows.anchor: أي : الزلزلة الشديدة وهكذا في سورة العنكبوت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the earth shook and severe heat struck; a cloud appeared, they sought its relief, and punishment poured on them there with Gabriel's cry.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : رجفت بهم الأرض وأصابهم حر شديد فرفعت لهم سحابة فخرجوا إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their دار is their town; Hud's parallel says في ديارهم.
rows.anchor: أي : صاروا في مدينتهم وفي سورة هود

rows.speaker: الحدادي
rows.claim: Al-Haddadi places them under the cloud near their homes, dead on faces and knees, fixed in place with no escape, as in the Canopy Day punishment.
rows.anchor: قال الحدادي : أي بقرب دارهم تحت الظلة كما قال تعالى : {فأخذهم عذاب يوم الظلة}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says they burned beneath the cloud and became ash-like bodies lying on the ground.
rows.anchor: وروي أنهم احترقوا تحت السحابة فصاروا ميتين بمنزلة الرماد الجاثم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second Ibn Abbas report says heat drove them into houses without relief; they welcomed a cool cloud, then God burned them beneath it and shook the earth until they became ash like fried locusts.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : فتح الله عليهم بابا من جهنم فأرسل عليهم منه حرا شديدا

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading says stubbornness made them see truth as falsehood and success as loss; their bodily end mirrored their inner state, spirits squatting in bodily abodes.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : من عنادهم رأوا الحق باطلا والباطل حقا والفلاح خسرانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause resumes the account to explain the consequence of their threat to expel Shuayb and the believers.
rows.anchor: استئناف لبيان ابتلائهم بشؤم قولهم فيما سبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were eradicated as if never resident there; punishment inverted their threat, leaving them expelled forever. مغنى means dwelling, and غنينا بمكان means residing there.
rows.anchor: أي : استأصلوا بالمرة وصاروا كأنهم لم يقيموا بقريتهم أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deniers and the arrogant may prevail briefly, but their fame and traces disappear, while truth's followers ultimately prevail.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن المكذبين والمتكبرين وإن كانت لهم غلبة في وقتهم ولكن تنقضي أيامهم بسرعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Masnavi verses recall deniers publicly and urge choosing the victorious side rather than allying with the defeated.
rows.anchor: يك مناره در ثناى منكران كودرين عالم كه تاباشد عيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second resumption says they were punished for their final statement and lost worldly and religious life, unlike Shuayb's followers; emphasis replaces an explicit rescue statement, as in 11:58.
rows.anchor: استئناف آخر لبيان ابتلائهم بعقوبة قولهم الأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After they perished, Shuayb turned away, said he had delivered God's messages and advised them, and lamented them deeply.
rows.anchor: قاله عليه السلام بعدما هلكوا تأسفا بهم لشدة حزنه عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آسى means intense grief; it is the first-person imperfect of أسى.
rows.anchor: فهو مضارع متكلم من الأسى من باب علم وهو شدة الحزن

rows.speaker: اليافعي
rows.claim: Al-Yafi‘i's verse advises withdrawing from people and taking God as companion, since human hearts resemble scorpions when examined.
rows.anchor: تجدهم عقاربا كذا في "روض الرياحين" لليافعي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God dispersed the Israelites across regions so none was free of them, completing the consequence of turning from truth and ensuring they could never gather strength again.
rows.anchor: أي : فرقنا بني إسرائيل {في الأرض} وجعلنا كل فرقة منهم في قطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أمما is a circumstantial accusative modifying قطعناهم, or a second object because the verb implies جعلناهم.
rows.anchor: حال من مفعول قطعناهم أي : حال كونهم جماعات أو مفعول ثان لقطعنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous among them are the religiously observant adherents of Moses' religion.
rows.anchor: وهم المتدينون بدين موسى {ومنهم دون ذالك}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase expands to ومنهم ناس دون ذلك: an omitted noun meaning people below that level is the subject and منهم a fronted predicate.
rows.anchor: تقديره ومنهم ناس دون ذلك

rows.speaker: التفتازاني
rows.claim: Al-Taftazani says grammarians parse such paired adverbials with the first as predicate and second as subject, supplying an omitted noun, though reversal is less apt in meaning.
rows.anchor: قال التفتازاني : قد شاع في الاستعمال وقوع المبتدأ والخبر ظرفين واستمر النحاة على جعل الأول خبرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ذلك can function like plural أولئك and point to the righteous, since a singular demonstrative may be used for duals and plurals.
rows.anchor: وجوز بمعنى أولئك فالإشارة إلى الصالحين وقد ذكر النحويون أن اسم الإشارة المفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hopes they will stop and turn from unbelief and disobedience; blessings encourage obedience and hardships warn against sin.
rows.anchor: {لعلهم يرجعون} ينتهون فيرجعون عما كانوا عليه من الكفر والمعاصي

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says they should have thanked for blessings but became arrogant, and been patient in hardship but insulted God, claiming He was poor and His hand bound; they failed the test.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (ايشانرا درنعمت شكر بايست كرد بطر واستغنا ظاهر كردند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian poem says the touchstone of experience exposes whoever has lied.
rows.anchor: خوش بود كر محك تجربه آيدبميان تاسيه روى شودهركه دروغش باشد

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading treats blessings as good works and self-admiration, as with Iblis; misdeeds become occasions for remorse, repentance, fear, and reverence, as with Adam returning to God in 7:23.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {وبلوناهم بالحسنات} أي : بكثرة الطاعات ورؤيتها والعجب بها كما كان حال إبليس {والسيئات} أي : المعاصي
